- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 10-day moving average), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward correction in forecast.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model forecasts are flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days of true values show strong downward trend, model often fails to capture early reversal; add 1–2 days of upward correction in forecast horizon.
- If sentiment history shows rapid shift from negative to positive (e.g., 0.14 → 0.95), model often misses the turn; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment momentum shift within 2–3 days.
